0.label: coiled_serpent_lid_apex
0.description: The raised roundel at the top of the drawn lid: a spiral with two small marks near its centre, set in a hatched ring, at the point where all the lid's compartments meet.
0.iconography: Most likely a coiled snake with its head at the centre — the serpent coil that guards lids and thresholds in Yoruba carving and belongs to the ouroboros / renewal family. A plain turned knob is the alternative.

panel.title: Survey drawing of a lidded vessel: coiled serpent over a lid of scenes
panel.object_type: pen-and-ink survey drawing of a lidded round container
panel.summary: A Frobenius survey drawing (sheet '5.') of a round lidded container in three-quarter view. The lid is divided into wedge-shaped compartments of figures and animals around a coiled apex; the body is panelled with rows of small triangles.

register_readings.reading: Lid compartments (undetected): figures with raised arms, a figure leaning over a quadruped, a tortoise, reclining figures and animals.
Body (undetected): panels of triangle rows between plain fillets.

panel.composition: Concentric and radial: an abstract centre, a ring of scenes, a patterned skirt.
panel.narrative: A container whose lid gathers people and animals — offerings, perhaps a hunt or tribute — around a coiled serpent. Such lidded bowls held kola or divination materials; placing the contents under a guardian coil fits that use. A pencilled word at the lower right (struck through) is not legible enough to read.
panel.hypotheses: Neutral. The triangle rows on the body are regular but read as texture.
uncertainties: A drawing of an object, so detail is the draughtsman's; the one box covers only the apex.
